hook.text: UN sanctions on Iraq in the 1990s aimed to weaken Saddam. Instead, 500,000 children died from malnutrition.

buildup.text: Economic sanctions restrict trade to pressure governments. But the pain falls on civilians, not leaders.

discovery.text: Leaders hoard scarce resources for elites and the military. Ordinary people absorb the deprivation first.

twist.text: North Korea has survived decades of sanctions while its people starve. The regime adapts; the people can't.

climax.text: Targeted 'smart sanctions' try to hit leaders, not populations. But leakage to civilians is unavoidable.

punchline.text: Sanctions are a weapon that hits everyone but its target.

quiz.question: Why do broad economic sanctions often fail to change government behavior?
options: Leaders are exempt from international sanctions
Leaders hoard resources; civilians absorb the pain
